---
title: Writing pages
description: The Markdown that smalldocs reads, each feature with its source and its result.
order: 3
---

smalldocs reads CommonMark with the parts of Pandoc's Markdown that websites use. Each section below
shows the source and then the result.

## Text

Quotes curl and dashes join, as Pandoc's `smart` does: "quoted" -- an en dash, --- an em dash,
and an ellipsis... Footnotes are numbered[^1]. ~~Strike~~ text, and `code`.

[^1]: A footnote goes to the end of the page.

Term
: A definition list gives each term its definition.

- [x] A task list
- [ ] with boxes

## Headings and attributes

A heading's id is made as Pandoc makes it, so links written for Quarto still work. Give your own id
and classes in braces:

```markdown
## Install it {#install .important}
```

A link, a picture, a span or inline code takes attributes too: `[text](url){.btn .btn-primary}`,
`![alt](pic.png){width=50%}`, `[red]{.text-danger}`. Here is a button: [A button](get-started.qmd){.btn .btn-primary .btn-sm}
and a [span with a class]{.text-danger}.

## Divs

A fence of colons makes a div. A fence with attributes opens one; a bare fence closes the innermost,
so divs nest with fences of one length:

```markdown
::: {.border .p-3}
Outer.

::: {.text-center}
Inner, centred.
:::
:::
```

::: {.border .p-3}
Outer.

::: {.text-center}
Inner, centred.
:::
:::

## Callouts

```markdown
::: {.callout-note}
A note, with the default title.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## A tip with its own title
The first heading in a callout becomes its title.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Folded" collapse="true"}
This warning opens when you click its title.
:::
```

::: {.callout-note}
A note, with the default title.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## A tip with its own title
The first heading in a callout becomes its title.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="Folded" collapse="true"}
This warning opens when you click its title.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
Important, and below it a caution.
:::

::: {.callout-caution appearance="simple"}
A caution with `appearance="simple"`.
:::

## Tabs

The headings in a `panel-tabset` div become tabs:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Python

```python
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    "Say hello."
    return f"Hello, {name}!"
```

## Shell

```bash
for name in Ann Bo; do echo "Hello, $name!"; done
```

## Prose

Tabs hold any Markdown.
:::

## Code

Code is highlighted with Pygments, in the classes Quarto uses, so the colours match. A copy button
shows on hover. A `filename` goes above the code:

```{.python filename="hello.py"}
import sys

def main() -> int:
    for arg in sys.argv[1:]:
        print(arg.upper())  # one line each
    return 0
```

A cell such as ```` ```{python} ```` is shown as code. smalldocs runs no code, so it shows no output;
it drops the `#|` lines and honours `echo: false`.

## Raw HTML

HTML in the Markdown passes through, and so does a block marked `{=html}`:

```{=html}
<p class="text-success">This paragraph came from a raw HTML block.</p>
```

## Figures

A picture alone in its paragraph, with alt text, becomes a figure, and the alt text its caption:

![The smalldocs mark, drawn as an SVG.](../images/mark.svg){width=120px}

## Tables

| Feature | Quarto | smalldocs |
|---|---|---|
| Pipe tables | yes | yes |
| Grid tables | yes | no: write a pipe table |
| `\|` in a cell | yes | yes |

## Maths

Inline maths goes between dollars, $e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0$, and display maths between double dollars:

$$
\int_0^1 x^2 \, dx = \frac{1}{3}
$$

A dollar followed by a space or a digit is money, not maths: it costs $5 and $10. With
`from: markdown-tex_math_dollars` in `format.html`, dollars are always dollars. KaTeX draws the maths,
and is loaded only on pages that have some.

## Diagrams

A `mermaid` block is drawn by mermaid.js, loaded only on pages that have one:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[_quarto.yml] --> B(smalldocs render)
  C[pages] --> B
  B --> D[_site]
```

## Shortcodes

smalldocs replaces these shortcodes, outside code blocks:

| Shortcode | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `{{</* include _part.qmd */>}}` | The file, without its front matter |
| `{{</* meta title */>}}` | An option of the page: {{< meta title >}} |
| `{{</* var version */>}}` | A value from `_variables.yml` |
| `{{</* env HOME */>}}` | An environment variable |

To show a shortcode as it is, put `/*` and `*/` inside its braces, as the left column of this table
does in its source.
